contracts.commit_point: The `await api.create_ticket(...)` call inside the create_ticket tool body (hr_harness/hr_harness/scenario/tools/tickets.py:65-71), which performs the external HR API mutation.
contracts.declared_mechanism: HumanInTheLoopMiddleware(interrupt_on={"create_ticket": {"allowed_decisions": ["approve", "reject"]}}, description_prefix="Подтвердите создание заявки") registered in the middleware chain of build_scenario_executor, interrupting before the create_ticket tool executes; the resume path in EpisodeManager.resume builds Command(resume={"decisions": [{"type": "approve"} | {"type": "reject", "message": ...}]}) for waiting_approval episodes; the episode graph runs with durability="sync" (both ainvoke and astream paths) so the checkpoint holding the decision is written before side effects; the tool passes idempotency_key=f"{configurable.thread_id}:{tool_call_id}" to api.create_ticket so a post-resume restart of the tools node cannot create a second ticket.
contracts.forbidden_condition: Committing the external ticket-creation effect (await api.create_ticket(...)) without a prior explicit employee decision resumed via Command(resume={"decisions": [...]}) — the tool contract states the ticket is created only after employee confirmation — or committing a duplicate ticket for the same (thread_id, tool_call_id) pair when the tools node restarts after the interrupt/resume cycle.

HumanInTheLoopMiddleware library internals (exact interrupt payload schema, whether reject definitively prevents the tool body from executing) are external dependency code not supplied.

Whether a checkpointer is guaranteed non-None in production (build_scenario_executor accepts BaseCheckpointSaver | None) — the durability='sync' checkpoint ordering presumes a checkpointer is present.
contracts.protected_operation: Execution of the create_ticket agent tool body within the scenario executor graph, culminating in the external HR API ticket-creation call.
contracts.protected_resource: External HR ticket system: ticket/request records created on specialist groups (canonical ids in TICKET_GROUPS) via HRApi.create_ticket.
contracts.protection_obligation: The external support-ticket creation performed inside the create_ticket agent tool (the api.create_ticket call) must not commit unless an explicit employee approve/reject decision has been captured via the HumanInTheLoopMiddleware interrupt on the create_ticket tool and durably checkpointed (durability="sync") before the side effect; additionally, when the tools node restarts after resume, the same tool call must not produce a second ticket (idempotency_key derived from thread_id + tool_call_id). (Merges the two reviewer phrasings, which describe the same obligation: first-phase 'external create_ticket forbidden without explicit user approve/reject decision' and second-phase 'HRApi.create_ticket must not commit without explicit employee approve decision'.)
scope_limits: Applies only to the tool named 'create_ticket' within the executor graph compiled by build_scenario_executor; the other pause point (ask_employee) uses a separate interrupt mechanism (executor.py:8-9).

Gate semantics (interrupt before tool execution, decision schema, reject bypassing the tool body) are declared to and enforced by the external HumanInTheLoopMiddleware library; only its registration and the resume-side decision construction are visible in the supplied source.
Idempotency is delegated to HRApi via idempotency_key=f"{thread_id}:{tool_call_id}"; the supplied source shows only key construction, not dedupe enforcement.

durability="sync" is applied at the episode-run level for both the ainvoke path (episodes.py:242) and the astream path (episodes.py:260); it governs checkpoint ordering for the whole episode run, not only create_ticket.

The middleware binds by tool name; the scoped_tools middleware only filters model-visible tools while ToolNode keeps the full catalog (executor.py:86-94), so create_ticket remains dispatchable regardless of tool_scope.
Expired episodes (TTL) have their checkpoint sub-threads deleted best-effort (episodes.py:308-318), so unresumed waiting_approval states are abandoned rather than executed later.
This obligation is separate from the verbatim_guard (log-only, executor.py:117-132) and ToolErrorMiddleware (excludes interrupt tools, executor.py:158-167), which are not part of this contract.
